title: Music Video Editing in DaVinci Resolve with Claude
goal: Finish editing a music video for social media
context: For this project, I will be editing a music video for social media. The purpose of the video is marketing for a company that helps women find confidence in their life through mindset shifts, daily habits around health and movement, and connecting with your inner-child.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: No, the task is a bit too complicated to finish in only an hour

Step 1.step_name: Upload videos from my phone into DaVinci
Step 1.step_action: I'll transfer the appropriate videos from my phone to DaVinci

nodes.label: Open DaVinci Resolve project and import phone video clips
nodes.detail: Opens the "Soeurs-Music-Video" project, starting from an empty Media Pool, and begins importing her media, saying "the first thing is just importing my media in." She drags in a batch of IMG_xxxx.mp4 phone clips from her Downloads folder.
nodes.softwares: DaVinci Resolve - Media Pool, File Explorer

nodes.label: Remove duplicate clips from the Media Pool
nodes.detail: Notices she has some duplicates among the imported clips and goes through the Media Pool getting rid of them.

nodes.label: Close other programs, then plan a bin structure by song section and usability
nodes.detail: Closes other applications on her computer because it's running slow. She then plans how she'll organize the clips into bins for what she expects to be a movie/music-video style edit, organized by the different parts of the song. She first plans to sort clips into usable versus not usable, but reconsiders deleting/marking anything as "not usable" since she might use them later, and starts to describe an alternative approach instead.
nodes.softwares: DaVinci Resolve - Media Pool, Windows desktop

Step 4.step_action: Download music, upload to resolve, and determine beats to pace clips to

nodes.label: Find and convert song via YouTube/Y2Mate
nodes.detail: In Chrome she searches YouTube for "gwen stefani sweet escape", confirms the official "Gwen Stefani - The Sweet Escape ft. Akon" video, then uses a Y2Mate-style YouTube-to-MP3 converter site to download the audio and decide which part of the song to use.

nodes.label: Import song onto Audio 1 track
nodes.detail: She imports the downloaded "Gwen Stefani - The Sweet Escape ft. Akon.mp3" file into the Media Pool's Music bin and drags it onto the Audio 1 track of the DaVinci timeline.
nodes.softwares: DaVinci Resolve - Edit page, Media Pool

nodes.label: Ask Claude about high-pitched audio
nodes.detail: Noticing the imported song sounds unusually high-pitched, she opens a new Claude chat and asks "I imported music into Davinci, the sound is more high pitched than it should be, could this be because it's stereo vs mono", starting the chat later titled "DaVinci audio pitch issue with stereo import".

nodes.label: Explain sample-rate mismatch as pitch cause
nodes.detail: Claude explains that a stereo/mono mismatch wouldn't cause a pitch shift but a sample-rate mismatch would, and walks her through checking File > Project Settings > Master Settings against the source file's sample rate to find and fix the discrepancy.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Explain sample-rate mismatch as pitch cause
Check the video on Youtube and download from Y2Mate
Import the download mp3 and edit the video
Follow up asking how to make the song less sharp
nodes.detail: She replies "OKay I think it's just the song that's a bit weird, is there a way to make it sound less sharp", reframing it as a tone/EQ issue rather than a technical pitch bug.

nodes.label: Recommend EQ cuts for harshness
nodes.detail: Claude suggests using Fairlight's EQ to cut harsh frequencies in the 2-8kHz range, roll off highs above 8-10kHz with a high-shelf, or apply a low-pass filter or de-esser, favoring small 2-3dB cuts over boosts.

nodes.label: Place beat markers along the music track
nodes.detail: Deciding the pitch/EQ fine-tuning is more of a final-touch item, she sets it aside and instead scrubs through the song placing markers on the Audio 1 track to mark where different clips should land, noting she must do this manually since she doesn't have DaVinci's paid auto beat-detection.

Step 2.step_name: Watch videos and tag key moments
Step 2.step_action: For this part, I'll go through the videos I have and sort them based on how they fit into the video. I'll use markers to tag specific parts that I think are "usable"

nodes.label: Organize footage into bins while reviewing lighting
nodes.detail: She sorts clips in the Media Pool into named bins ("Usable"/"Not", "Woohoo section", "Music section", "Lyrics", "Filler") while watching through her footage and thinking about lighting/color consistency and which parts of each clip are usable.

nodes.label: Cross-reference footage against beat markers
nodes.detail: She reviews clips in the source viewer against the beat markers she placed earlier on the music track, judging which usable segments of footage line up well with specific beats in "The Sweet Escape".

nodes.label: Rough-place clips on Video 1 track
nodes.detail: She begins dragging video clips onto the Video 1 timeline track in rough general positions aligned to the music's beat markers, explicitly noting these placements are not final, just to orient herself with the footage she has to work with.

Step 3.step_action: Edit the video clips for consistent lighting, quality, and frame size using DaVinci's Color page

nodes.label: Build color-correction node tree
nodes.detail: She moves to the Color page and begins building a node tree (labeled WB, exposure, reds, greens) on the first clip, planning to match clips shot in similar lighting and copy/paste grades across them for efficiency. Partway through, DaVinci becomes laggy with the node tree active and she has to reload the project.

nodes.label: Ask Claude for the add-node shortcut
nodes.detail: She switches to the Claude chat and types "davinci add node shortcut" to speed up building out her node tree.

nodes.label: List node shortcut keys
nodes.detail: Claude lists the Color page node shortcuts (Alt+S serial, Alt+P parallel, Alt+L layer, Alt+O outside, Alt+C copy grade) and notes they can vary by keyboard preset (Resolve vs Final Cut vs Avid style).

nodes.label: Ask Claude for a warmer look without the Temp slider
nodes.detail: She asks Claude "color grading settings for warmer lut without using temp slider" while working on the node tree in the Color page.

nodes.label: Suggest warming techniques beyond Temp
nodes.detail: Claude lists alternatives to warm the image: pushing Gain/Gamma color wheels toward orange, using the Hue vs Hue curve, the RGB Mixer, or pulling down the Blue custom curve, recommending a subtle Gamma push plus a small Blue curve pull-down as the most natural combo.

nodes.label: Review Claude's warming suggestions and reduce red saturation
nodes.detail: She asks Claude "color grading settings for warmer lut without using temp slider" while working on the node tree in the Color page.
nodes.softwares: Claude chat, DaVinci Resolve - Color page

nodes.label: Ask Claude which wheel controls black hardness
nodes.detail: Continuing to grade, she asks Claude "which wheel affects black hardness" to get harder, more contrasty shadows in a clip.

nodes.label: Explain Lift wheel and contrast controls
nodes.detail: Claude explains the Lift wheel controls the black point/shadow region, with lowering it crushing blacks harder, and points to the Contrast/Pivot sliders and the Luma custom curve for more surgical control over shadow hardness.

nodes.label: Continue refining grades across clips
nodes.detail: She keeps refining the white balance, exposure, reds, and greens nodes across multiple clips in the node tree, using the Hue vs Sat curve tool repeatedly while commenting that her computer is struggling and lagging noticeably as she applies the edits.

Step 5.step_action: Choosing which video clips should go where and piecing it all together + exporting it with the right settings for Instagram

nodes.label: Ask Claude for Instagram vs YouTube export settings
nodes.detail: She returns to the "DaVinci audio pitch issue with stereo import" Claude chat and asks "davinci export setting for instagram vs youtube".

nodes.label: Provide platform-specific export presets
nodes.detail: Claude gives detailed settings: Instagram MP4/H.264 at 1080x1920 (9:16), 8,000-12,000 kb/s, AAC 320kb/s; YouTube MP4/H.264 at 1920x1080 (16:9) with similar bitrate guidance and higher rates for 4K, noting Resolve has a built-in YouTube preset.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Provide platform-specific export presets
Edit the export settings
nodes.detail: Switches to DaVinci's Deliver page and opens the Render Settings / Render Queue panels to begin configuring the final export.

nodes.label: Ask about exporting via QuickTime
nodes.detail: She asks Claude "what about quicktime, I've used that before and had good qualityu", recalling better results from a past QuickTime export.

nodes.label: Explain ProRes/QuickTime vs H.264 tradeoffs
nodes.detail: Claude explains QuickTime likely looked better because it used ProRes as a mastering codec versus H.264's delivery compression, gives ProRes 422 HQ settings for a high-quality master, and notes YouTube/Instagram will recompress any upload anyway.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Explain ProRes/QuickTime vs H.264 tradeoffs
Ask if Encoding Profile should be High
nodes.detail: Back in the H.264 export settings, she asks Claude "Should encoding profile be high".

nodes.label: Confirm High profile is correct
nodes.detail: Claude confirms High profile is the modern default with the best compression efficiency and universal compatibility, and briefly explains the associated Level setting (4.1/4.2 for 1080p).

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Confirm High profile is correct
Question why encoding profile was omitted
nodes.detail: She asks "why didn't you tell me that before" about the missing profile advice.

nodes.label: Acknowledge the omitted encoding profile
nodes.detail: Claude acknowledges the earlier omission was a real gap.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Acknowledge gap and confirm Balanced is fine
Ask whether balance preset okay
Balance is a reasonable choice
Review Claude's response about Balance is a reasonable choice
Question the 80,000 kb/s bitrate field
nodes.detail: Noticing the bitrate field in Render Settings reads 80,000 kb/s, she asks Claude "so 80000 bitrate is good?".
nodes.softwares: DaVinci Resolve - Deliver page, Claude chat

nodes.label: Flag 80,000 kb/s as excessive for 1080p
nodes.detail: Claude explains 80,000 kb/s is way overkill for 1080p (8,000-12,000 kb/s is the sweet spot), still high but closer to reasonable for 4K (35,000-45,000 recommended), and only normal at 8K or high-motion HDR; it asks what resolution she's exporting at to confirm.

nodes.label: Reply with export resolution
nodes.detail: She replies "1080p 16x9 vertical", combining a landscape aspect ratio label with a vertical orientation.

nodes.label: Clarify orientation and confirm bitrate range
nodes.detail: Claude flags that 16:9 (landscape, 1920x1080) and vertical/9:16 (1080x1920) are opposites and asks her to double check which she actually set up, then confirms that either way at 1080p she should drop the bitrate to 8,000-12,000 kb/s since anything above that is wasted data the platforms will compress away.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Clarify orientation and confirm bitrate range
Render final video with recommended export settings
nodes.detail: She configures the final render as MP4/H.264 with High profile and 12,000 kb/s based on the accumulated Claude recommendations, adds the job to the Render Queue, starts the render, and confirms the video finishes exporting successfully.
